BURSEVI:v4p173/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p173/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p173/r1.claim: The survivor was the cupbearer; ‘remembered’ derives from idh-tadhakkara, with tāʾ changed to dāl and assimilated with dhāl, meaning he recalled Joseph.
BURSEVI:v4p173/r1.anchor: وادكر أصله اذتكر فقلبت التاء دالا والذال دالا وأدغمت

BURSEVI:v4p173/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p173/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p173/r2.claim: ‘After an ummah’ means after a long period, here seven years; the clause is circumstantial, and the long period resembles a collective of many days and hours.
BURSEVI:v4p173/r2.anchor: بعد أمة أي مدة طويلة حاصلة من اجتماع الأيام الكثيرة

BURSEVI:v4p173/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p173/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v4p173/r3.claim: The king was bewildered by his dream; seeing this, the cupbearer remembered Joseph and his interpretation and offered to bring the answer.
BURSEVI:v4p173/r3.anchor: أي تذكر الناجي يوسف وتأويله رؤياه ورؤيا صاحبه وطلبه أن يذكره عند الملك

BURSEVI:v4p173/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p173/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p173/r4.claim: The cupbearer asked permission to go to prison because Joseph, a wise man of Jacob’s family, had previously interpreted their dreams.
BURSEVI:v4p173/r4.anchor: فأرسلوه إلى يوسف فأتاه فاعتذر إليه وقال

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر وعكرمة ومجاهد والضحاك وقتادة
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r6.claim: These readers say وادكر بعد أمه, meaning after forgetfulness; al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī instead reads بعد إمة, meaning after a blessing.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r6.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة ابن عباس وابن عمر بخلاف وعكرمة ومجاهد بخلاف

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r1.claim: الأمه means forgetfulness, while الإمة means a blessing, so the two readings give different accounts of what followed Joseph's rescue.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r1.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: "الأمه": النسيان، أمه الرجل يأمه أمها: أي نسي

QIRAAT-ER:12:45:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:10#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:10#1/r1.claim: The standard canonical recitation has a short final vowel form.
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:10#1/r1.anchor: Standard canonical reading with hamza maqṭūʿa — short final vowel form in recitation

QIRAAT-ER:12:45:10#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:10#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:10#2/r1.claim: A canonical option extends the final ā with madd.
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:10#2/r1.anchor: Canonical reading with madd extension — long ā final vowel before hamza in liaison

QIRAAT-ER:12:45:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:15#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:15#1/r1.claim: The standard seven-reader form elides the first-person suffix yāʾ at pause.
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:15#1/r1.anchor: yāʾ of 1S suffix elided at pause — standard recitation convention

QIRAAT-ER:12:45:15#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:15#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:15#2/r1.claim: The ten-reader form retains the full first-person yāʾ object pronoun.
QIRAAT-ER:12:45:15#2/r1.anchor: Reading 10: full yāʾ retained throughout — overt 1S object pronoun

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the cupbearer remembered Joseph after a period of time.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r1.anchor: عن الثوري عن عاصم عن أبي رزين عن ابن عباس ﴿ وادكر بعد أمة ﴾ قال بعد حين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the cupbearer remembered after forgetting Joseph.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وادكر بعد أمة ﴾ قال بعد نسيانه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r3.claim: Hasan also glosses umma as a period of time.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#2/r3.anchor: قال معمر وقال الحسن بعد حين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r1.claim: After the dream stumped the king's court, the cupbearer remembered Joseph and his own and companion's interpretations after a long interval; أمّة means a long period and the clause is circumstantial.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r1.anchor: لما استثنى الملك في رؤياه وأعضل على الملأ تأويلها، تذكر الناجي من القتل وهو ساقي الملك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r2.claim: The common reading ادكر derives from اذْتكر by changing and assimilating consonants; al-Ḥasan reads واذكر with a different assimilation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r2.anchor: وادكر أي تذكر ما سبق له مع يوسف بعد أمة أي: مدة طويلة. والجملة من قوله وادكر حالية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r3.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r3.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads after immah with kasra on the hamza, meaning after the blessing of surviving execution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي: بعد إمة بكسر الهمزة أي: بعد نعمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains the blessing as God drawing Joseph near to release and cites a poem using immah for blessing or good fortune.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: بعد نعمة أنعم الله بها على يوسف في تقريب إطلاقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r5.claim: Yughāth may derive from rescue and relief or from rain; an Arab woman says the latter form when asking for rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r5.anchor: يغاث: يحتمل أن يكون من الغوث وهو الفرج، يقال: أغاثهم الله فرج عنهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r1.claim: Immah with fatḥa on hamza means blessing or a good condition; readers transmit forms with an open hamza, a light mīm, or a still mīm.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن علي والضحاك وقتادة وأبو رجاء وشبيل بن عزرة وربيعة بن عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r2.claim: These readers use after ummah with fatḥa on hamza, a light mīm, and hāʾ; similar readings are variously reported from Ibn ʿUmar, Mujāhid, and ʿIkrima.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس، وزيد بن علي، والضحاك، وقتادة، وأبو رجاء، وشبيل بن عزرة الضبعي، وربيعة بن عمرو: بعد أمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r3.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد وشبيل بن عزرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r3.claim: They also read ummah with a still mīm as an irregular verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r3.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة وأيضا مجاهد، وشبيل بن عزرة: بعد أمه بسكون الميم، مصدر أمه على غير قياس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the still-mīm reading an error; Abū Ḥayyān objects that he habitually labels readings erroneous.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ومن قرأ بسكون الميم فقد أخطأ انتهى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r5.claim: The cupbearer says he will report the interpretation from someone who possesses its knowledge, not from himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r5.anchor: أنا أنبئكم بتأويله أي أخبركم به عمن عنده علمه لا من جهتي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads أنا أتيكم, from the verb meaning to come, as also found in the codex.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن أنا أتيكم مضارع أتى من الإتيان، وكذا في الإمام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r7.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r7.claim: Ubayy's codex adds فأرسلون, meaning send me to Joseph and allow me to ask for an interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r7.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي: فأرسلون، أي ابعثوني إليه لأسأله، ومروني باستعباره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Joseph's prison was outside the king's city; another report places it inside the city, with a present-day site identified by the Nile eight miles from Fusṭāṭ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r8.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: كان في السجن في غير مدينة الملك، وقيل: كان فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r9.claim: The narrative elides the dispatch and arrival: the king sends the cupbearer to Joseph, who then addresses him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r9.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف التقدير: فأرسلوه إلى يوسف فأتاه فقال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r10.claim: Ṣiddīq is an intensive form; the cupbearer calls Joseph that after knowing him for a long time and testing his truthfulness in both dream interpretations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p284/r10.anchor: والصديق بناء مبالغة كالشريب والسكير، وكان قد صحبه زمانا وجرب صدقه

AKHFASH:v1p398/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p398/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p398/r2.claim: وادكر is form VIII from ذكرت, underlyingly اذتكر; adjacent sounds assimilate, but dāl preserves voicing instead of ta, and ṭāʾ is avoided because it is emphatic.

AKHFASH:v1p398/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p398/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p398/r3.claim: Some say مذكر, replacing tāʾ with dhāl before assimilation.
AKHFASH:v1p398/r3.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم (مذكر) فابدل التاء ذالا ثم ادخل الذال فيها.

AKHFASH:v1p398/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p398/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p398/r4.claim: In the reading أن يصلحا, ṣād does not assimilate into tāʾ because of voicing and emphasis; tāʾ becomes ṣād instead, while يصطلحا is the better form.
AKHFASH:v1p398/r4.anchor: فابدلوا التاء صادا وقال بعضهم (يصطلحا) وهي الجيدة.

FARRA:v2p46/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p46/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p46/r3.claim: الأمة means a span of time; another reading أمه means forgetfulness, from the verb أمه, and مأموه describes one lacking sense.
FARRA:v2p46/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر عن بعضهم (بعد أمه) وهو النسيان

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218/r1.claim: Umma means a period of time, said here to be seven years.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218/r1.anchor: {وادكر بعد أمة} أي: بعد حين. يقال: بعد سبع سنين.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218/r2.speaker: قراء
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218/r2.claim: A reading with amatin means after forgetting.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ (بعد أمة) أراد: بعد نسيان (1) .

ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r1.claim: The survivor is Joseph's cupbearer. Most read وادكر with dāl, from a form where t assimilated to d; al-Hasan reads اذكر with ذ assimilated to ذ, while the first reading is more eloquent. Both mean recalling Joseph.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r1.anchor: أي صاحبي يوسف عليه السلام وهو الشرابي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r2.claim: After a long interval, after umma means after a span or community of time.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r3.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r3.claim: Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli reads إمة as a favor: release from the threat of execution and prison, and the king's beneficence toward the cupbearer; a verse illustrates this usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r3.anchor: بكسر الهمزة وتشديد الميم أي نعمة عليه بعد نعمة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes the favor as God's favor on Joseph by bringing his release near, but Al-Alusi considers this interpretation far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r4.anchor: المراد بعد نعمة أنعم الله تعالى بها على يوسف عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, Zayd ibn Ali, Mujahid, Ikrima, and Shubayl ibn Azra are reported to read with a light, open form from a verb meaning to forget; Al-Alusi dismisses those who rejected this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن عباس وزيد بن علي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r6.claim: The phrase after a long time is parenthetical between the speech verb and its content; it could be circumstantial with an understood قد, but joining it to the relative clause is rejected because the later remembering is new information, not a known description.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r6.anchor: والجملة اعتراض بين القول والمقول وجوز أن تكون حالا من الموصول

ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r7.claim: The cupbearer offers to inform them through access to someone who knows the interpretation, not from his own knowledge; he says send me so they will dispatch him to Joseph.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r7.anchor: أي أخبركم بتأويل ذلك الذي خفى أمره بالتلقي ممن عنده علمه لا من تلقاء نفسي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r8.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r8.claim: Al-Hasan reads أنا آتيكم, 'I will bring you,' instead of 'I will inform you'; when corrected, he asks whether Joseph himself had been informing them.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ عن الحسن أنه كان يقرأ أنا آتيكم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r9.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r9.claim: Ubayy is also reported to read أنا آتيكم; al-Bahr says this is likewise the reading in the codex.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وغيره عن أبي أنه قرأ أيضا كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r10.claim: The plural imperative send me can address only the king as an honorific plural; a report says the cupbearer knelt and asked that the king send him to a knowledgeable man in prison. Ibn Abbas says the prison was outside the king's city, while another view puts it inside; Al-Alusi leaves its actual location to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p253/r10.anchor: وضمير الجمع إما لأنه أراد الملك وحده لكن خاطبه بذلك على سبيل التعظيم

MAJAZ:v1p312/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p312/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p312/r4.claim: Waddakara derives from dhakartu; the tāʾ assimilated into dhāl and became a doubled dāl.
MAJAZ:v1p312/r4.anchor: «وادكر بعد أمة» (45) أي افتعل من ذكرت فأدغم التاء فى الذال فحولوها دالا ثقيلة

MAJAZ:v1p312/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p312/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p312/r5.claim: Some read baʿda umma, meaning after a period; others read baʿda amah, meaning after forgetting, from amih meaning he forgot.
MAJAZ:v1p312/r5.anchor: «بعد أمة» أي بعد حين، وبعضهم يقرؤها بعد أمه، أي بعد نسيان، ويقال: أمهت تأمه أمها، ساكن، أي نسيت.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p246#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p246#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p246#2/r1.claim: The one who survived execution is the cupbearer; he remembered Joseph’s request after a period of seven years.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p246#2/r1.anchor: {وقال الذي نجا} من القتل، {منهما} من الفتيين وهو الساقي، {وادكر} أي: تذكر قول يوسف اذكرني عند ربك،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p246#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p246#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p246#2/r2.claim: The cupbearer asked permission to inform the king, with the omitted sense “send me to him”; Ibn Abbas says the prison was outside the city.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p246#2/r2.anchor: وفيه اختصار تقديره: فأرسلني أيها الملك إليه، فأرسله

NAHHAS:v2p331/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p331/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p331/r2.claim: ادكر derives from إذتكر; voiced ذ cannot assimilate to unvoiced ت, so it changes to د; أمه يأمه means to forget.
NAHHAS:v2p331/r2.anchor: والذال قريبة المخرج من التاء ولم يجز إدغامها فيها لأن الذال مجهورة

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r1.claim: The person who escaped was the cupbearer, Joseph's fellow prisoner; he remembered Joseph after a long stretch of time.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r1.anchor: { وقال الذي نجا منهما } من صاحبي السجن وهو الشرابي. { وادكر بعد أمة } وتذكر يوسف

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r2.claim: The reading ummah can mean a long period, a favor after his rescue, or forgetfulness; the clause is an intervening remark and the cupbearer's speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r2.anchor: بكسر الهمزة وهي النعمة أي بعدما أنعم عليه بالنجاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r3.claim: He offered to tell the king's council the interpretation and asked them to send him either to the person who knew it or to the prison.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:45/r3.anchor: { أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون } أي إلى من عنده علمه أو إلى السجن.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r1.claim: The cupbearer remembered Joseph after a long, accumulated span of time; “remembered” is parsed as a form meaning he sought remembrance.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r1.anchor: أي طلب الذكر - بالمعجمة , وزنه افتعل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r2.claim: The cupbearer confidently offers to report the dream’s interpretation and asks the court to send him to Joseph.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r2.anchor: { أنا أنبئكم } أي أخبركم إخبارا عظيما

DURR-FULL:v4p543/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the cupbearer remembered Joseph after a period of time; Mujahid, Hasan, Ikrima, Ibn Kathir, and al-Suddi likewise say after a while or years.
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وادكر بعد أمة} قال: بعد حين

DURR-FULL:v4p543/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r5.claim: In another gloss, Ibn Abbas and Saʿid ibn Jubayr say the cupbearer remembered Joseph after years.
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - في قوله {وادكر بعد أمة} يقول: بعد سنين

DURR-FULL:v4p543/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r6.claim: Hasan read the phrase as after a group of people.
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r6.anchor: عن الحسن - رضي الله عنه - أنه قرأ {وادكر بعد أمة} قال: بعد أمة من الناس

DURR-FULL:v4p543/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas gives a reading with fatḥa and lightening of the form, interpreting it as after forgetfulness.
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - أنه قرأ {وادكر بعد أمة} - بالفتح والتخفيف يقول بعد نسيان

DURR-FULL:v4p545/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r1.speaker: عكرمة والحسن وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r1.claim: These authorities read after umma as after forgetfulness.
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r1.anchor: عكرمة والحسن وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك - رضي الله عنهم - أنهم قرأوا {بعد أمة} أي بعد نسيان

DURR-FULL:v4p545/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r2.claim: Mujahid read the verb with jussive ending and a softened consonant.
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r2.anchor: عن حميد - رضي الله عنه - قال: قرأ مجاهد رضي الله عنه {وادكر بعد أمة} مجزومة مخففة

DURR-FULL:v4p545/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's reading has the cupbearer say that he will come to you with its interpretation.
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r3.anchor: عن هرون - رضي الله عنه - قال في قراءة أبي بن كعب / أنا آتيكم بتأويله /

DURR-FULL:v4p545/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r4.claim: A further reading also has أنا آتيكم بتأويله; its reciter defended it by asking whether the cupbearer was actually informing them.
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r4.anchor: أنه كان يقرأ / أنا آتيكم بتأويله / فقيل له: أنا انبئكم قال: أهو كان ينبئهم

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r1.claim: Nabū remembered Joseph when he heard the king's request for an interpretation, recalling Joseph's accurate interpretations for him and his companion.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ، عن مجاهد قال : فلما سمع نبو من الملك ما سمع منه ومسالته ، عن تاويلها ، ذكر يوسف ، وما كان عبر له ولصاحبه

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r2.claim: “After an ummah” means after a period of time.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس وادكر بعد امة قال بعد حين

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r3.claim: The phrase means after a period, the term of which is known to God.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي ورق عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس وادكر بعد امة قال بعد حين وهو : الاجل الذي يعلمه الله

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : وادكر بعد امة يقول : بعد سنين

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r5.claim: The phrase means after an age or long stretch of time.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد يقول الله : وادكر بعد امة اي : بعد حقبة من الدهر

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas recited “after forgetfulness,” which Qatada explains as after forgetting.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ، عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس انه قرا : وادكر بعد امة ويفسرها قتادة : بعد نسيان

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r7.claim: Hasan recited the phrase as “after a people.”
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة ، عن الحسن انه قرا : وادكر بعد امة قال : بعد امة من الناس

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r8.claim: Hasan recited “I will come to you with its interpretation”; when corrected to “I will inform you,” he asked whether Joseph was their prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2151#2/r8.anchor: قال مالك بن دينار : وكان الحسن يقرا هذه الاية انا اتيكم بتاويله فقيل له : يا أبا سعيد انا انبئكم بتاويله

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2152/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2152/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2152/r1.claim: The prison was outside the city, so the cupbearer went out to Joseph.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2152/r1.anchor: عن السدي قوله : انا انبئكم بتاويله فارسلون قال ابن عباس : لم يكن السجن في المدينة فانطلق الساقي إلى يوسف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r5.claim: When the courtiers could not interpret the dream, the cupbearer remembered Joseph and offered to explain it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r5.anchor: فلما ظهر عوص تعبير هذا الحلم تذكر ساقي الملك ما جرى له مع يوسف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r6.claim: Starting with “I” and making himself the subject attracts the king's surprise and strengthens the claim that he can explain a baffling dream.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r6.anchor: وابتداء كلامه بضميره وجعله مسندا إليه وخبره فعلي لقصد استجلاب تعجب الملك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r7.claim: Calling himself the one who will inform them is figurative because he is the cause of the explanation; “send me” seeks the king's permission to leave his presence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r7.anchor: مجاز عقلي لأنه سبب الإنباء ، ولذلك قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r8.claim: His confidence that Joseph remained in prison suggests it was a private prison: any release or death would have reached the king and his court.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p282/r8.anchor: ولعل سبب يقينه ببقاء يوسف عليه السلام في السجن أنه كان سجن الخاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr derives ادكر from اذتكر: the infix ت becomes د for ease and proximity of articulation, then ذ assimilates into the lighter د; this is the most eloquent substitution.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r1.anchor: أصله : اذتكر ، وهو افتعال من الذكر ، قلبت تاء الافتعال دالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r2.claim: The Prophet is reported to have recited the related form مدكر in Q 54:15, as found in the Ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r2.anchor: وهو قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله تعالى : { فهل من مدكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r3.claim: Ummah here means a long period, originally the span in which a generation dies out; a generation itself can be called an ummah, as in Q 3:110 on one interpretation referring to the Companions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r3.anchor: والأمة : أطلقت هنا على المدة الطويلة ، وأصل إطلاق الأمة على المدة الطويلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r4.claim: Calling the period an ummah exaggerates how long the cupbearer forgot Yusuf; the Torah gives the interval as two years.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r4.anchor: وإطلاقه في هذه الآية مبالغة في زمن نسيان الساقي . وفي التوراة كانت مدة نسيانه سنتين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r5.claim: The plural address in “inform you” and “send me” is directed to the king as an honorific plural, comparable to Q 23:99.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r5.anchor: ضمائر جمع المخاطب في أنبئكم } { فأرسلون } مخاطب بها الملك على وجه التعظيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r6.claim: The cupbearer leaves the recipient unnamed so the news of Yusuf's interpretation can surprise the court and land with greater force; a prisoner was not expected to have such skill.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p283/r6.anchor: ولم يسم لهم المرسل إليه لأنه أراد أن يفاجئهم بخبر يوسف عليه السلام بعد حصول تعبيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r1.claim: Muddled dreams and inner thoughts are disregarded; a true vision is what can be interpreted and investigated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r1.anchor: فالأحلام وحدثان النفس ملغاة، والرؤيا هي التي تعبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r5.claim: The surviving cupbearer remembered Joseph after hearing the king and courtiers discuss the dream.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r5.anchor: تذكر يوسف وعلمه بتأويل الأحلام والرؤى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r6.claim: Iddakkara derives from idtakara, with consonant changes and assimilation; other Arabic forms and Qur’anic readings show the same alternation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r6.anchor: من الذكر، قلبت التاء دالا وأدغم الأول في الثاني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r7.claim: The majority read baʿda ummah as after a period of time.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and others read ummah as forgetfulness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وجماعة «بعد أمة» وهو النسيان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r9.speaker: مجاهد وشبل بن عزرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r9.claim: Mujahid and Shibl ibn ʿUzra read ummah with a still mīm, as a verbal noun meaning forgetting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r9.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وشبل بن عزرة «بعد أمه» بسكون الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r10.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r10.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqayli reads immah as a blessing and interprets the phrase as God’s favor in bringing Joseph near release and honor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r10.anchor: بعد نعمة أنعمها الله على يوسف في تقريب إطلاقه وعزته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r11.claim: The verb remembered strengthens the reading that the forgotten person in the earlier story was Joseph and the forgetter was the cupbearer, though the issue remains open.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r12.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r12.claim: The majority read أنا أنبئكم, while al-Hasan and Ubay’s codex have أنا آتيكم.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r12.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن: «أنا آتيكم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r13.claim: Fa-arsilūn is a request for permission to go; Ibn Abbas says the prison was outside the king’s city, while others place it within the city.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r13.anchor: كان السجن في غير مدينة الملك- قاله ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r14.claim: The author notes that people in his own day identify Joseph’s prison beside the Nile, eight miles from Fustat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p248/r14.anchor: ويرسم الناس اليوم سجن يوسف في موضع على النيل بينه وبين الفسطاط ثمانية أميال

SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r1.claim: وادكر is most likely circumstantial from the relative pronoun or its referent, the subject of نجا; it may alternatively coordinate with نجا.
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وادكر }: فيه وجهان، أظهرهما: أنها جملة حالية: إما من الموصول

SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r2.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r2.claim: The common ادكر is from اذتكر: tāʾ becomes dāl after ذال and the neighboring consonants assimilate; al-Hasan reads with ذال instead, as in مدكر at 54:15.
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r2.anchor: والعامة على " ادكر " بدال مهملة مشددة وأصلها: اذتكر افتعل من الذكر

SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r3.claim: The common reading أمة has a damma, doubled mīm and tanwin, meaning a long period.
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r3.anchor: والعامة على " أمة " بضم الهمزة وتشديد الميم وتاء منونة، وهي المدة الطويلة

SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r4.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r4.claim: Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli reads إمة with kasra, interpreted as a blessing; al-Zamakhshari cites Adi's line as evidence.
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r4.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي بكسر الهمزة، وفسروها بالنعمة

SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن علي وقتادة والضحاك وأبو رجاء
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r5.claim: They read أمه with an open hamza, light mīm, and hāʾ tanwin, deriving it from أمه, forgetfulness.
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وزيد بن علي وقتادة والضحاك وأبو رجاء " أمه " بفتح الهمزة وتخفيف الميم

SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r6.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة وشبيل بن عزرة
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r6.claim: They read بعد أمه with a still mīm as a nonstandard verbal noun of أمه, forgetfulness.
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r6.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وعكرمة وشبيل بن عزرة: " بعد أمه " بسكون الميم

SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports that some grammarians call the still-mīm reading erroneous; the author says Zamakhshari only attributes the criticism to others and an authentic reading cannot be wrong.
SAMIN-DURR:12:45/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ومن قرأ بسكون الميم فقد خطىء ". قال الشيخ: " وهذا على عادته

SAMIN-DURR:12:45#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:45#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:45#2/r1.claim: أنا أنبئكم is the clause quoted after the statement verb.
SAMIN-DURR:12:45#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { أنا أنبئكم } هذه الجملة هي المحكية بالقول. وقرأ العامة من الإنباء.

SAMIN-DURR:12:45#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:45#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:12:45#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan reads أنا آتيكم from أتى, a meaning close to أنا أنبئكم.
SAMIN-DURR:12:45#2/r2.anchor: والحسن " أنا آتيكم " مضارع أتى من الإتيان، وهو قريب من معنى الأول.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r1.claim: The man who survived the two prisoners was the cupbearer, who remembered Joseph and what he had asked.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r1.anchor: يعني اللذي تخلص من القتل من الفتيين وهو الساقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says iddākara derives from idhtakara: tā changes to dāl and dhāl assimilates into dāl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج وأصل ادكر اذتكر ولكن التاء أبدلت منها الدال وأدغمت الذال في الدال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reads the word with a doubled dhāl rather than dāl.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r4.claim: “After an ummah” means after a period—the time Joseph had remained in prison after the cupbearer left.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r4.anchor: وقوله ( بعد أمة ) أي بعد حين وهو الزمان الذي لبثه يوسف بعده في السجن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r5.claim: Ibn Abis and al-Hasan read ummah as ammah, meaning after forgetfulness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عابس والحسن بعد أمة أراد بعد نسيان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r6.claim: If Joseph was the one who forgot God, the verb may simply mean “remembered,” as Arabic sometimes uses a form without implying a prior opposite action.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r6.anchor: معنى قوله وادكر ذكر كما تقول العرب احتلب بمعنى حلب واغتدى بمعنى غدا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r7.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the cupbearer delayed mentioning Joseph because he feared the king would recall the offense that had led to his imprisonment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231/r7.anchor: إنما لم يذكر الساقي خبر يوسف للملك حتى احتاج الملك إلى تأويل رؤياه خوفا من أن يكون ذكره ليوسف سببا لذكره الذنب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r1.claim: The cupbearer says he will tell the king the dream's interpretation through Joseph.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ( أنا أنبئكم بتأويله ) أي من جهة يوسف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r2.speaker: يعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r2.claim: Ya'qub keeps the final yāʾ in “send me” in both connected and paused reading, as in two other verses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r2.anchor: أثبت الياء فيها وفي ( ولا تقربون ) [ يوسف 60 ] ( أن تفندون ) [ يوسف 94 ] يعقوب في الحالين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r3.claim: The plural address “send me” may honor the king alone or address him together with his attendants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p231#2/r3.anchor: فخاطب الملك وحده بخطاب الجميع تعظيما وقيل خاطبه وخاطب أتباعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r3.claim: The rescued prisoner remembered Yusuf after a lapse of time and offered to explain the dream; a variant reading takes ummah to mean forgetfulness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r3.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم: "بعد أمة" أي: بعد نسيان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r4.claim: The king sent the former prisoner to Yusuf, who addressed him as truthful and heard the king's dream without reproaching him for forgetting or demanding release first.

JISHUMI:v5p3652/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r6.claim: They read بعد أمه as after forgetfulness, deriving the word from a verb meaning to forget; Abū ʿUbayd cites a poem using this sense.
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك: بعد [أمه] بفتح الألف

JISHUMI:v5p3652/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r7.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r7.claim: Mujāhid reads بعد أمه with the mīm still and says the forms are dialects meaning forgetfulness.
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r7.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد: بعد أمه بسكون الميم وفتح الألف والهاء الخالص، وهما لغتان

JISHUMI:v5p3652/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r8.speaker: أبو الهيثم
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r8.claim: Abū al-Haytham considers the still-mīm form correct and the form with fatḥa on mīm an error; another grammarian allows the latter for forgetfulness.
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r8.anchor: قال أبو الهيثم: إنما هو (أمه) بجزم الميم، (وأمه) بفتحها خطأ

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r3.claim: وادكر بعد أمة means that the cupbearer remembered after a time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r3.anchor: يعني بعد حين , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r4.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r4.claim: وادكر بعد أمة means that he remembered after forgetting.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r5.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r5.claim: وادكر بعد أمة may mean that he remembered after a community of people had passed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r5.anchor: بعد أمة من الناس , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r6.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says Joseph entered the well at seventeen, spent eighty years in servitude, prison, and kingship, was reunited with his family, and lived twenty-three more years.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r6.anchor: ألقي يوسف في الجب وهو ابن سبع عشرة سنة , وكان في العبودية والسجن والملك ثمانين سنة وجمع له شمله فعاش بعد ذلك ثلاثا وعشرين سنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r7.claim: A reading has أمة with a fatḥa on alif and light m; al-amma in this light form means forgetfulness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r7.anchor: وقرىء { وادكر بعد أمة } بفتح الألف وتخفيف الميم , والأمه : بالتخفيف النسيان

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r8.claim: The cupbearer promises to identify someone who knows the dream's interpretation, but initially does not name Joseph.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r8.anchor: أي أخبركم بمن عنده علم بتأويله ثم لم يذكره لهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the prison was outside the city; the cupbearer went to Joseph after receiving permission, four years after their separation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لم يكن السجن بالمدينة فانطلق إلى يوسف حين أذن له وذلك بعد أربع سنين

MUQATIL:12:43-46/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:43-46/r3.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:12:43-46/r3.claim: Muqatil reports Gabriel told Joseph he would leave prison the next day; Joseph asked about Jacob, whose grief had blinded him, and was told his reward equaled that of one hundred martyrs.
MUQATIL:12:43-46/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: قال له: أيها الملك الحسن وجهه، الطيب ريحه، الطاهر ثيابه، الكريم على ربه، أي رسل ربي أنت؟

MUQATIL:12:43-46/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:43-46/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:43-46/r4.claim: The cupbearer remembered Joseph's accurate interpretation of his and the baker's dreams and offered to find the interpretation for the king.
MUQATIL:12:43-46/r4.anchor: فلما سمع الساقي رؤيا الملك، ذكر تصديق عبارة يوسف، عليه السلام، في نفسه، وفي الخباز، فذلك قوله:

NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r1.claim: The survivor was spared execution; after a long interval he recalled Joseph when the king's dream baffled the court and asked to be sent to him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r1.anchor: بعد مدة طويلة وذلك أنه حين استفتى الملك فى رؤياه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r2.claim: Wād-dakara is the eloquent reading, derived from idh-takara with substitutions and assimilation; Hasan's wa-dhkur is explained as remembering Joseph and what he had witnessed.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r2.anchor: بالدال هو الفصح وأصله إذتكر فأبدلت الذال دالا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r3.claim: Hasan reads wa-dhkur, meaning the survivor remembered Joseph and what he had seen; Yaʿqub reads 'send me' with yāʾ.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r3.anchor: وعن الحسن واذكر ووجه أنه قلب التاء ذالا وأدغم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r4.claim: The survivor says he can report its interpretation from the person who knows it and asks to be sent to Joseph.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p191#2/r4.anchor: أنا أخبركم به عمن عنده علمه ﴿ فأرسلون ﴾ وبالياء يعقوب أى فابعثونى إليه

ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r4.claim: After umma means after a time; Ibn ʿAbbās reads wa-adhkur baʿda amah, with amah meaning forgetfulness.
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r4.anchor: أي بعد حين، وقرأ ابن عباس: واذكر بعد أمه

ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r5.claim: The reading amah with a still mīm, attributed by some to Abū ʿUbayda, is not correct; the verbal noun is amah with fatḥa.
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r5.anchor: وروى بعضهم عن أبي عبيدة: أمه بسكون الميم

ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r6.speaker: الحسن
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ‘I will bring you its interpretation,’ but the author dislikes it for differing from the codex.
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: أنا آتيكم بتأويله، وأكرهها

ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r7.claim: Iddakkara derives from idh-takara, with tāʾ replaced by dhāl and the two dhāls assimilated into dāl; wa-adhkur is possible, but dāl is better.
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r7.anchor: أصله واذتكر، ولكن التاء أبدل منها الذال

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r1.claim: The man who survived was the king's cupbearer; after a period of time he remembered Joseph and his request, with ummah meaning a stretch of time.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r1.anchor: وقال الذي نجا منهما } يعني ساقي الملك. «وادكر بعد أمة» أي بعد حين، عن ابن

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r2.speaker: ابن درستويه
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r2.claim: Ibn Durustawayh says ummah means a period only through an omitted word, such as a period or span of time; ummah also means a large group of people.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r2.anchor: وقال ابن درستويه: والأمة لا تكون الحين إلا على حذف مضاف، وإقامة المضاف إليه مقامه

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r3.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash says ummah is singular in form but plural in meaning, and each animal species is a community; a hadith exempts dogs from a command to kill them because they are a community.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r3.anchor: الأخفش: هو في اللفظ واحد، وفي المعنى جمع وكل جنس من الحيوان أمة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r4.claim: A hadith says that if dogs were not a community among communities, the Prophet would have ordered them killed.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r4.anchor:
وفي الحديث:
" لولا أن الكلاب أمة من الأمم

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r5.claim: The cupbearer remembered Joseph's request to mention him before the king.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r5.anchor: وادكر } أي تذكر حاجة يوسف، وهي قوله: «اذكرني عند ربك

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r6.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and al-Dahhak has أمة with an open hamza and light m, meaning after forgetting; other readings use أمه for forgetfulness, while al-Ashhab reads إمة, meaning after a favor.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r6.anchor: أمة } ، بفتح الهمزة وتخفيف الميم أي بعد نسيان

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r7.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r7.claim: Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli reads إمة, meaning the cupbearer remembered after God granted him the favor of survival.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي «بعد إمة» أي بعد نعمة أي بعد أن أنعم الله عليه بالنجاة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r8.claim: Some say the cupbearer forgot because God's decree required Joseph to remain imprisoned; another says he remembered but feared reminding the king of the crime that had jailed him.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r8.anchor: ثم قيل: نسي الفتى يوسف لقضاء الله تعالى في بقائه في السجن مدة. وقيل: ما

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r9.claim: The root of ادكر is اذتكر; because ذال is voiced and تاء unvoiced, the latter changes to دال and assimilation yields ادكر.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r9.anchor: أصل ادكر اذتكر والذال قريبة المخرج من التاء ولم يجز إدغامها فيها لأن الذال مجهورة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r10.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r10.claim: Al-Hasan reads أنا آتيكم بتأويله; al-Nahhas says the standard أنبئكم is also correct and means I will tell you when asked.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «أنا آتيكم بتأويله» وقال: كيف ينبئهم العلج؟ قال النحاس: ومعنى: «أنبئكم» صحيح حسن

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r11.claim: فأرسلون addresses the king in an honorific plural or the king and his assembly; Yusuf and الصديق are singular forms, with صديق meaning very truthful.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r11.anchor: فأرسلون } خاطب الملك ولكن بلفظ التعظيم، أو خاطب الملك وأهل مجلسه. { يوسف } نداء مفرد، وكذا

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r12.claim: The cupbearer asked to be sent to Joseph and then returned to the king and his companions, either to explain the dream or show Yusuf's knowledge and secure his release; people may refer to the king alone as an honorific.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45-46/r12.anchor: أفتنا } أي فأرسلوه، فجاء إلى يوسف فقال: أيها الصديق! وسأله عن رؤيا الملك

RAZI-FULL:v18p118#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p118#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p118#2/r2.claim: The cupbearer recalled Joseph because he believed Joseph was deeply learned in dream interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v18p118#2/r2.anchor: فعند هذه المقالة تذكر ذلك الشرابي واقعة يوسف فإنه كان يعتقد فيه كونه متبحرا في هذا العلم

RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r1.claim: The cupbearer tells the king that Joseph is virtuous, pious, and learned, and that his earlier interpretations for him and the baker were completely accurate.
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r1.anchor: إن في الحبس رجلا فاضلا صالحا كثير العلم كثير الطاعة قصصت أنا والخباز عليه منامين

RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r2.claim: Al-Hasan's reading uses ذال in واذكر, meaning he remembered; the source calls the dāl reading in وادكر more eloquent.
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r2.anchor: { وادكر } بالدال هو الفصيح عن الحسن

RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r3.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r3.claim: Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli reads ʾimma, meaning favor or blessing, and the verse of Adi ibn Zayd uses it alongside prosperity and kingship.
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r3.anchor: قرأ الأشهب العقيلي { بعد أمة } بكسر الهمزة والإمة النعمة

RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r4.claim: He gives three senses of الأمة: a long period, favor or blessing, and forgetfulness; readings vary in the vowel on the word's mīm.
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r4.anchor: الأول : { بعد أمة } أي بعد حين

RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says اذّكر can mean to mention or report and does not prove the cupbearer had forgotten Joseph.
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r5.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري : اذكر بمعنى ذكر وأخبر

RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r6.claim: The cupbearer may have concealed Joseph from the king out of fear that recalling the offense behind his imprisonment would worsen matters; alternatively, both men forgot.
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r6.anchor: فلعل الساقي إنما لم يذكره للملك خوفا من أن يكون ذلك اذكارا لذنبه

RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r7.claim: Fa-arsilūn may address the king with a plural form of respect or address the king and his court.
RAZI-FULL:v18p119/r7.anchor: خطاب إما للملك والجمع أو للملك وحده على سبيل التعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v18p120/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p120/r1.claim: The cupbearer hopes to return with Joseph's interpretation so the people will recognize his learning; he speaks cautiously because all the other interpreters failed and he might fail too.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120/r1.anchor: فالمراد لعلي أرجع إلى الناس بفتواك لعلهم يعلمون فضلك وعلمك

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

ASAD-NOTES:12:44#n46/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:44#n46/r1.speaker: almost all authorities
ASAD-NOTES:12:44#n46/r1.claim: The word ummah here means a time or a long period of time.
ASAD-NOTES:12:44#n46/r1.anchor: According to almost all the authorities, the noun ummah denotes here "a time" or "a long period of time"

ASAD-NOTES:12:44#n47/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:44#n47/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:44#n47/r1.claim: The cup-bearer addresses the whole assembly, not only the King, explaining the plural pronoun.
ASAD-NOTES:12:44#n47/r1.anchor: the cup-bearer obviously addresses the assembly as a whole, and not the King alone

STUDYQURAN:12:45/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:45/r1.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:12:45/r1.claim: The wine carrier remembered Joseph’s words from 12:42.
STUDYQURAN:12:45/r1.anchor: The wine carrier remembered Joseph’s words in v. 42 (Bg)

STUDYQURAN:12:45/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:45/r2.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:12:45/r2.claim: After a while means seven years, matching Joseph’s imprisonment in 12:42.
STUDYQURAN:12:45/r2.anchor: After a while refers to a period of seven years (Bg), which corresponds to the length of time Joseph spent in prison

STUDYQURAN:12:45/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:45/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:45/r3.claim: The wine carrier persuaded the king to consult Joseph by citing Joseph’s earlier accurate dream interpretation.
STUDYQURAN:12:45/r3.anchor: by pointing to his own experience with Joseph’s powers of dream interpretation

TAB-FULL:v13p188/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p188/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p188/r1.claim: The surviving cupbearer says he will report the dream's interpretation and asks to be released to go to the person who knows it. The narrative omits that they released him and he went to Yusuf.

TAB-FULL:v13p188/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p188/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p188/r2.claim: Ummah here means a long period or epoch; Ibn Ishaq's account identifies the survivor as Nabu, who remembered Yusuf after a long interval and brought him the king's dream.
TAB-FULL:v13p188/r2.anchor: {وادكر بعد أمة} [يوسف: 45] : أي حقبة من الدهر

TAB-FULL:v13p188/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p188/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p188/r3.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Abbas says the prison was outside the city, explaining the cupbearer's request to be sent to Yusuf.
TAB-FULL:v13p188/r3.anchor: عن السدي، " {وقال الذي نجا منهما وادكر بعد أمة أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون} [يوسف: 45] قال ابن عباس: لم يكن السجن في المدينة

TABATABAI:12:41-42/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:41-42/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:41-42/r8.claim: The later statement that the cupbearer remembered Joseph after a lapse of years confirms that the cupbearer, not Joseph, was the one who forgot.
TABATABAI:12:41-42/r8.anchor: قرينة صالحة على أن الناسي هو الساقي دون يوسف

TABATABAI:12:45-46/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r1.speaker: الملأ
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r1.claim: The officials tell the king that the vision is a jumble of dreams and that they cannot interpret this kind of mixed dream.
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r1.anchor: قالوا أي قال الملأ للملك ما رأيته أضغاث أحلام وأخلاط من منامات مختلفة

TABATABAI:12:45-46/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r2.speaker: الملأ
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r2.claim: An alternative reading is that the officials cannot interpret dreams generally, or that they know only how to interpret true dreams.
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r2.anchor: أو وما نحن بتأويل جميع المنامات بعالمين وإنما نعلم تأويل الرؤى الصالحة

TABATABAI:12:45-46/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r3.claim: Umma here means a span of years: the period during which the cupbearer forgot to mention Joseph to his lord after Joseph asked him to do so.
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r3.anchor: والمراد بها ههنا الجماعة من السنين وهى المدة

TABATABAI:12:45-46/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r4.claim: The survivor is the cupbearer, who recalls Joseph’s request after years and offers to bring the interpretation of the king’s dream from him in prison.
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r4.anchor: وقال الذي نجا من السجن من صاحبي يوسف فيه وادكر بعد جماعة من السنين ما سأله يوسف

TABATABAI:12:45-46/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r5.claim: The plural address in I will inform you and send me includes the officials around the king, who manage affairs of state; the later reference to returning to the people supports this.
TABATABAI:12:45-46/r5.anchor: تشريك لمن حضر مع الملك وهم الملأ من أركان الدولة

TABRISI:12:43-49/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن عمر، الضحاك، قتادة، زيد بن علي
TABRISI:12:43-49/r3.claim: A noncanonical reading uses بعد أمه, with هā, and is attributed to these readers, with disagreement in the transmissions from Ibn Abbas and Ibn ʿUmar.
TABRISI:12:43-49/r3.anchor: في الشواذ قراءة ابن عباس وابن عمر بخلاف والضحاك وقتادة وزيد بن علي

TABRISI:12:43-49/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49/r4.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
TABRISI:12:43-49/r4.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqayli reads بعد أمة with kasra on the hamza.
TABRISI:12:43-49/r4.anchor: وقراءة الأشهب العقيلي بعد أمة بكسر الهمزة

TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r5.claim: Iddikār comes from remembrance: its original tāʾ changes to dāl and assimilates with dhāl; the alternative اذكر is possible, though dāl is better.
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r5.anchor: وأصله اذتكار لكن التاء أبدل منها الدال وأدغمت الذال في الدال

TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r6.claim: Umma may mean a group united in purpose or a period of time; ṣiddīq means strongly affirming the truth or especially truthful.
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r6.anchor: والأمة الجماعة تؤم أمرا والأمة المدة وهي الجملة من الحين

TABRISI:12:44-46/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:44-46/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد، قتادة
TABRISI:12:44-46/r8.claim: After a long time, the escaped cupbearer remembered Yusuf and what he had instructed him; the account is attributed to these authorities.
TABRISI:12:44-46/r8.anchor: تذكر شأن يوسف وما وصاه به بعد حين من الدهر وزمان طويل عن ابن عباس

THALABI:v5p226/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p226/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p226/r3.claim: The surviving cupbearer remembered Joseph’s request after a long period and offered to interpret the dream; umma means a stretch of time.
THALABI:v5p226/r3.anchor: أي وتذكر حاجة يوسف قوله: اذكرني عند ربك

THALABI:v5p226/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p226/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك
THALABI:v5p226/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and al-Dahhak read the phrase as after forgetfulness; Arabic also uses umma for forgetting.
THALABI:v5p226/r4.anchor: قراء ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك [بعد أمة] أي بعد نسيان

THALABI:v5p226/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p226/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v5p226/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda cites a poem using amihat to mean forgetting, supporting the lexical reading.
THALABI:v5p226/r5.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيدة: أمهت وكنت لا أنسى حديثا

THALABI:v5p226/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p226/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p226/r6.claim: Mujahid reads amih with a still mīm and open initial vowel, another form for forgetfulness.
THALABI:v5p226/r6.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد: أمه، بسكون الميم وفتح الألف وهاء لخالصة

THALABI:v5p226/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p226/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p226/r7.claim: The cupbearer asks to be released and authorized to go to Joseph; the verse omits the intervening journey to prison.
THALABI:v5p226/r7.anchor: فأرسلون: فأطلقوني، وأذنوا لي أمضي وآتيكم بتأويله وفي الآية اختصار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r1.claim: After the court failed to interpret the king's dream, the cupbearer recalled that Joseph had correctly interpreted his and the baker's dreams and asked permission to consult him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي (¬4): لما سأل الملك عن رؤياه، جثا الساقي بين يديه بعد انقضاء جواب الملأ،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r2.claim: The rescued man was one of the two servants, the one who dreamed of pressing wine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1): يريد أحد العبدين، وهو الذي رأى أنه يعصر خمرا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r3.claim: The word وادكر was discussed at the phrase فهل من مدكر in Sūrat al-Qamar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {وادكر} ذكرنا الكلام في هذا الحرف عند قوله: {فهل من مدكر} في سورة القمر (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r4.claim: ابن عباس, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and most commentators take بعد أمة to mean after a period of time; ʿAṭāʾ's report specifies years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3) والحسن (¬4) ومجاهد (¬5) وعامة أهل التفسير والمعاني (¬6): بعد حين.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan agrees that بعد أمة means after a period of time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3) والحسن (¬4) ومجاهد (¬5) وعامة أهل التفسير والمعاني (¬6): بعد حين.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid agrees that بعد أمة means after a period of time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3) والحسن (¬4) ومجاهد (¬5) وعامة أهل التفسير والمعاني (¬6): بعد حين.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r7.claim: Some language scholars take أمة as a portion or span of time, supported by its sense of a large group; Ibn ʿAbbās's report through ʿAṭāʾ says “after years.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r7.anchor: قال بعض أهل المعاني: هي الجملة من الحين، والجماعة من الحين؛ لأن الجماعة الكثيرة من الناس # أمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r8.claim: وادكر can mean “remembered and told,” just as reflexive forms such as احتلب and اعتدى can equal their simpler verbs; it does not prove earlier forgetfulness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري (¬2): يقال إذ ادكر بمعنى: ذكر وأخبر الملك، وصلح أن يكون ادكر بمعنى ذكر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r9.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r9.claim: Al-Kalbī, reporting Ibn ʿAbbās, says the cupbearer withheld Joseph's story for fear of reminding the king why he had been jailed; God decreed Joseph's continued stay.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r9.anchor: وقد قال الكلبي فيما روى عن ابن عباس (¬3): إنما لم يذكر الساقي خبر يوسف للملك حتى احتاج الملك إلى تعبير رؤياه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r10.claim: For those who take the forgetting as the cupbearer's, وادكر keeps its plain sense of remembering after forgetting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p131#2/r10.anchor: ومن نسب النسيان إلى الساقي] (¬4) فسر الادكار على ظاهره ولم ينقله إلى معنى الذكر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p133/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p133/r1.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p133/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads أنا آتيكم instead of أنا أنبئكم, intending the cupbearer to report the interpretation without saying it came from Joseph.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p133/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن (¬5) (أنا آتيكم بتأويله) وقال: أراد العلج ينبئهم بتأويله حتى لا يأتي به من عند يوسف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p133/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p133/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p133/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj dislikes that reading because it departs from the written consonantal text.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p133/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p133/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p133/r3.claim: فأرسلون addresses both the king and his court; plural address to the king alone is also possible because his companions share his view and command.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p133/r3.anchor: قال أبو بكر: هو خطاب للملك وملئه، لذلك خاطب بالجمع.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:45-46/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:45-46/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:45-46/r1.claim: The surviving cupbearer remembered Joseph after a long period and offered to obtain the interpretation from him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:45-46/r1.anchor: وتذكر أمر يوسف بعد حين من الدهر

ELMALILI:12:45-46/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:12:45-46/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:12:45-46/r1.claim: The survivor is the cupbearer who had asked Yusuf to interpret the dreams; after a long interval he remembered Yusuf and offered to explain the king's dream.
ELMALILI:12:45-46/r1.anchor: uzun bir müddet sonra -bu vesile ile- hatırlayıp dedi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:45/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:45/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:45/r1.claim: When the king’s interpreters failed to explain his dream, the surviving prison companion remembered Joseph, obtained permission to consult him, and brought back his interpretation of coming abundance, famine, and hardship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:45/r1.anchor: kâhinlerin, kralın rüyasını yorumlamaktan aciz kaldıklarını görünce, Hz. Yûsuf’u hatırladı ve gidip rüyayı ona yorumlatmak üzere izin istedi

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The words rendered as remembering are synonymous.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Ummah here means a period of time.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The word #%!ٌﻣﺔ means “a period of time.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The wine-server recalled Joseph's accurate interpretation of his own dream, which he had long forgotten to mention to the king.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The helplessness of the courtiers in interpreting the dream reminded the wine-server of Joseph’s skill in interpreting his own dream.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: He immediately offered to interpret the king's dream if allowed to visit Joseph.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he could interpret this dream for them if they allow him to go and meet Joseph (sws).

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r1.claim: Wad-dakara with dāl is the eloquent reading; al-Ḥasan reads wa-dhakara with dhāl, from the original tadhakkara.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r1.anchor: قرىء : ( وادكر ) بالدال وهو الفصيح . وعن الحسن : ( واذكر )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r2.claim: The rescued cupbearer remembered Joseph after a long interval, when the king’s dream baffled the court; he recalled Joseph’s successful interpretation and request to be remembered.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r2.anchor: بعد مدة طويلة ، وذلك أنه حين استفتى الملك في رؤياه وأعضل على الملأ تأويلها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r3.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r3.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads ʿimmah, “blessing”; ʿAdī’s poem witnesses this meaning for the word al-immah.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي ( بعد إمة ) بكسر الهمزة ، والإمة النعمة . قال عدي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r4.claim: Another reading, baʿda amihi, means “after forgetfulness”; reading the mīm with sukūn is an error.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r4.anchor: وقرىء : ( بعد أمه ) بعد نسيان . يقال : أمه يأمه أمها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r5.claim: The cupbearer says he will report the interpretation from someone who knows it; al-Ḥasan’s reading means “I will bring you its interpretation.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r5.anchor: عمن عنده علمه . وفي قراءة الحسن : ( أنا آتيكم بتأويله )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r6.claim: “Send me” asks the king’s party to dispatch him to Joseph so he can ask for an interpretation.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Joseph’s prison was not in the city.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p448/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : لم يكن السجن في المدينة

TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.claim: Al-Qummī reports the king’s dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows and seven green ears with dry ones; the cupbearer recalled it after a time, and Joseph interpreted seven plentiful years, seven famine years, then rain.
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.anchor: ثم إن الملك رأى رؤيا فقال لوزرائه إني رأيت في نومي سبع بقرات سمان

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p24/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p24/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p24/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads وادكر بعد أمة, while other reciters are said to read بعد أمة.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p24/r2.anchor: فابن عباس يقرأ: وادكر بعد أمة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p31/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p31/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p31/r3.claim: Category two changes meaning through case or stem vowels while leaving the written shape unchanged: the two forms in Sabaʾ, تلقونه, and أمة.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p31/r3.anchor: والوجه الثاني: أن يكون الاختلاف في إعراب الكلمة وحركات بنائها بما يغير معناها، ولا يزيلها عن صورتها في الكتاب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p33/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p33/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p33/r2.claim: وادكر بعد أمة means remembered after a period; بعد أمة can mean after forgetting. Both are true: Joseph was recalled after time and after being forgotten.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p33/r2.anchor: أي بعد حين، وبعد أمة أي بعد نسيان له، والمعنيان جميعا وإن اختلفا صحيحان

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248#2/r3.claim: أمة can mean a period: in 12:45 a while, and in 11:8 a limited number of years; the sense develops from the lifespan of a community.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248#2/r3.anchor: أي: سنين معدودة. كأن الأمة من الناس القرن ينقرضون في حين

MAJAZ:v1p12/r11.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p12/r11.speaker: بعضهم
MAJAZ:v1p12/r11.claim: Some recited وادكر بعد أمة, cited in the source as a variant wording.
MAJAZ:v1p12/r11.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم: وادكر بعد أمة» (22/ 45) ، وقرأها

MAJAZ:v1p14/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p14/r1.speaker: آخرون
MAJAZ:v1p14/r1.claim: Others explain بعد أمة as ‘after forgetfulness.’

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p896/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p896/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p896/r2.claim: مدّكر and يوسف’s وادّكر mean “remembered”: in the افتعل pattern, tāʾ changes to dāl beside dāl or dhāl, with the consonants assimilating; tāʾ similarly changes to ṭāʾ beside ṣād or ḍād.

NASHR:v2p296/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p296/r11.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v2p296/r11.claim: The two Medinans, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿĀmir open the yāʾs in آبائي إبراهيم and لعلي أرجع.
NASHR:v2p296/r11.anchor: آبائي إبراهيم لعلي أرجع فتحهما المدنيان، وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر

NASHR:v1p26/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p26/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p26/r1.claim: Some interpret seven, seventy, and seven hundred as figures for abundance rather than exact totals, and apply this to the seven Quranic ahruf and the hadith about faith's branches.
NASHR:v1p26/r1.anchor: والعرب يطلقون لفظ السبع والسبعين والسبعمائة ولا يريدون حقيقة العدد بحيث لا يزيد ولا ينقص

NASHR:v1p26/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p26/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p26/r2.claim: The author rejects a nonliteral count for the seven ahruf: reports say Gabriel brought one letter and kept asking for more until seven, and Abu Bakra understood Mikaʾil's silence to mark the final number.
NASHR:v1p26/r2.anchor: وفي حديث أبي بكرة: فنظرت إلى ميكائيل فسكت فعلمت أنه قد انتهت العدة

NASHR:v1p26/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p26/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p26/r3.claim: After surveying sound, anomalous, weak, and rejected readings, the author says their differences fall into seven kinds.
NASHR:v1p26/r3.anchor: تتبعت القراءات صحيحها وشاذها وضعيفها ومنكرها، فإذا هو يرجع اختلافها إلى سبعة أوجه

NASHR:v1p26/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p26/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p26/r4.claim: Type one changes vowels without changing meaning or written form; type two changes vowels and meaning but not the written form, as in إدكر بعد أمة.
NASHR:v1p26/r4.anchor: وذلك إما في الحركات بلا تغيير في المعنى والصورة: نحو (البخل) بأربعة (ويحسب) بوجهين

NASHR:v1p26/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p26/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p26/r5.claim: Type three changes letters and meaning without changing written form, as تبلو/تتلوا; type four changes the written form without changing meaning, as بصطة/بسطة and الصراط/السراط.
NASHR:v1p26/r5.anchor: وإما في الحروف بتغير المعنى لا الصورة نحو (تبلوا وتتلوا)

NASHR:v1p26/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p26/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p26/r6.claim: Type five changes both written form and meaning, as أشد منكم/منهم, يأتل/يتأل, and فامضوا إلى ذكر الله; type six changes word order.
NASHR:v1p26/r6.anchor: أو بتغيرهما نحو (أشد منكم، ومنهم) و (يأتل ويتأل)

NASHR:v1p26/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p26/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p26/r7.claim: Type seven adds or deletes letters or words, as أوصى/وصى and الذكر/الأنثى; pronunciation traits such as idgham, imala, and madd are not separate wording differences.
NASHR:v1p26/r7.anchor: أو في الزيادة والنقصان نحو (وأوصى ووصى) و (الذكر والأنثى)

NASHR:v1p26/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p26/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p26/r8.claim: Differences of recitation such as assimilation, imala, lengthening, tafkhim, and facilitation are performance qualities that do not create a distinct wording; if counted, they belong with the first category.
NASHR:v1p26/r8.anchor: وأما نحو اختلاف الإظهار، والإدغام، والروم، والإشمام، والتفخيم

NASHR:v2p180/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p180/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p180/r1.claim: The author counts 22 yāʾs of the first-person suffix, listing examples across suras, including حتى تؤتون in Yusuf.
NASHR:v2p180/r1.anchor: وياء المتكلم ثنتان وعشرون ياء: وهي في البقرة ياءان إذا دعاني

NASHR:v2p180/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p180/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p180/r2.claim: There are 86 yāʾs at verse ends: five are original and 81 are first-person suffixes; the Yusuf examples include فأرسلون، ولا تقربون، and لولا أن تفندون.
NASHR:v2p180/r2.anchor: وأما التي في رءوس الآي فست وثمانون ياء منها خمس أصلية

NASHR:v2p297/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p297/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p297/r1.claim: In Yusuf's six extra yāʾs, Yaʿqub retains فأرسلون، ولا تقربون، and أن تفندون in both connection and pause; Abu Jaʿfar and Abu Amr retain حتى تؤتون in connection, while Ibn Kathir and Yaʿqub retain it in both positions.
NASHR:v2p297/r1.anchor: فأرسلون، ولا تقربون، وأن تفندون، أثبتهن في الحالين يعقوب

NASHR:v2p297/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p297/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p297/r2.claim: Qunbul is reported, with disagreement from him, to retain the yāʾ in يرتع and من يتق ويصبر both in connection and pause.
NASHR:v2p297/r2.anchor: أثبتها قنبل بخلاف عنه في الحالين، وكذلك (من يتق ويصبر) لقنبل

NASHR:v1p27/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p27/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p27/r1.claim: Traits such as imala, tafkhim, idgham, and facilitation do not create a different wording or meaning; if counted as variation, they belong to the first category.
NASHR:v1p27/r1.anchor: فهذا ليس من الاختلاف الذي يتنوع فيه اللفظ والمعنى

NASHR:v1p27/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p27/r2.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
NASHR:v1p27/r2.claim: Al-Razi's seven groups are noun-number/gender forms, verb inflection and voice, case endings, addition or deletion, word order, substitution or reversal, and dialectal pronunciation differences.
NASHR:v1p27/r2.anchor: ثم رأيت الإمام الكبير أبا الفضل الرازي حاول ما ذكرته فقال

NASHR:v1p27/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p27/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
NASHR:v1p27/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba's first two groups distinguish case variation that leaves form and meaning unchanged from vowel or inflection changes that alter meaning without changing the written form.
NASHR:v1p27/r3.anchor: وقد تدبرت وجوه الاختلاف في القراءات فوجدتها سبعة

NASHR:v1p27/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p27/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
NASHR:v1p27/r4.claim: His next three groups cover letter changes affecting meaning but not written form, changes affecting both form and meaning, and changes in writing without meaning, as النشر/النشوز and طلع نضيد/طلح منضود.
NASHR:v1p27/r4.anchor: الاختلاف في حروف الكلمة دون إعرابها بما يغير معناها ولا يزيل صورتها

NASHR:v2p230#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p230#2/r1.speaker: المدنيان
NASHR:v2p230#2/r1.claim: The two Medinese readers retain alif in أنا before a following hamza with ḍamma or fatḥa, including أنا أنبئكم.
NASHR:v2p230#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان بإثباتها عند المضمومة والمفتوحة

NASHR:v2p230#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p230#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p230#2/r2.claim: Qalun has conflicting reports before kasra in إن أنا إلا: several transmitters retain alif, while others transmit deletion.
NASHR:v2p230#2/r2.anchor: واختلف عن قالون عند المكسورة نحو إن أنا إلا، فروى الشذائي عن ابن بويان

NASHR:v2p230#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p230#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p230#2/r3.claim: The retention route is transmitted by al-Shudhāʾi, Ibn Shanbudh, Ibn Mihran, Abu Marwan, Ibn Dhawaba by text, and Abu Awn through al-Hulwani.
NASHR:v2p230#2/r3.anchor: وكذلك روى ابن شنبوذ وابن مهران عن أبي حسان أيضا، وهي رواية أبي مروان عن قالون

NASHR:v2p230#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p230#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p230#2/r4.claim: Deletion is transmitted by al-Faradi through the Maghribi routes and Ibn al-Habbab through Ibn Buwyan; Ibn Dhawaba also reports deletion in performance, as do other transmitters.
NASHR:v2p230#2/r4.anchor: وروى الفرضي من طرق المغاربة، وابن الحباب عن ابن بويان حذفها

NASHR:v2p230#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p230#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p230#2/r5.claim: The author accepts both Qalun readings through Abu Nashit; through al-Hulwani he takes deletion, while Abu Awn's route allows both.
NASHR:v2p230#2/r5.anchor: والوجهان صحيحان عن قالون نصا وأداء نأخذ بهما من طريق أبي نشيط

NASHR:v2p230#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p230#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p230#2/r6.claim: Ibn Sawwar, Abu al-Ala, and others report retention from al-Faradi in al-Araf alone, not al-Shuara or al-Ahqaf; the author says he read this route through both transmitters.
NASHR:v2p230#2/r6.anchor: رويا من طريق الفرضي إثباتها في الأعراف فقط دون الشعراء والأحقاف

NASHR:v2p230#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p230#2/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p230#2/r7.claim: Other readers delete the alif in connected recitation in all three environments, but there is no disagreement about retaining it at a pause.
NASHR:v2p230#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بحذف الألف وصلا في الأحوال الثلاثة، ولا خلاف في إثباتها وقفا

NASHR:v2p230#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p230#2/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p230#2/r8.claim: The author cross-references earlier discussions of assimilation in لبثت/لبثتم, deletion of hāʾ in يتسنه for Yaʿqub, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf, and imala of حمارك.
NASHR:v2p230#2/r8.anchor: وتقدم اختلافهم في إدغام لبثت ولبثتم وإظهاره في باب حروف قربت مخارجها

TAB-FULL:v1p77#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p77#2/r1.speaker: شقيق
